questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

My mother (1)/ told me (2)/ not to eat the junk food. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The definite article '**the**' is used to refer to something in particular or definite. 

 
 
• When something in particular is referred to we should always use **the**. 
 
• But when talking about things in general, we should not use the definite article. 
 
• In the given sentence **junk food **is a very broad term and nothing particular is mentioned here. 
 
• If the **junk food **being talked about was from a specific or particular place or outlet we could have used **the**. 
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, **the **should be omitted. 
 
 
 
• The correct sentence is: My mother told me** not to eat junk food**. * *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the **junk food **being talked about was from a particular place **Ex**: Pizza Hut 
 
• Then we use '**the' **in the sentence. 
 
 
• My mother told me not to eat ***the junk food from Pizza Hut*** 
 
 
 
• Here we are talking about a particular junk food, hence we use the definite article.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Early marriages not only leads to high-population (1)/ and thwart the progress of our young population, (2)/ but also entail an enormous amount of trouble to young mothers. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error lies with plural verb.

By rule, when the subject is plural, the corresponding verb will be plural.

**Leads** should be changes to **lead.**

*Early marriages not only lead to high-population and thwart the progress of our young population but also entail an enormous amount of trouble to young mothers.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

There is a cat ______ the house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e.** 'In' **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context , it is stated about the location of cat.
 
• **In** is used **to indicate location or position within or inside something.**
 
 
• **For example**- We went for a swim **in** the lake.
 
 

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is - *There is a cat **in**__ the house.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **At**- Used to point out specific time, Indicate a place and to indicate an activity.

 
 
• **For example**- She stared at me.
 
 
 
• **For**- to talk about a purpose or a reason for something. 
 
 
• **For example**- I'm going for some breakfast.
 
 
 
• **Of**- to show that people or things relate to other things or people. 
 
 
• ​**For example**- He is a coworker of mine.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The rascal cheated him out of his money.

options.text: His money was cheated out by the rascal.
He was cheated out of his money by the rascal.
He was cheated out of money by the rascal.
Money was cheated by the rascal of him.

questions.solution: The given sentence is in the past tense. Thus, passive voice will be of the form **was/were + past participle of cheat = *cheated***. We cannot remove any information from the given sentence => rule out 3) ( doesn't say whose money). Option 2) is the correct answer.

questions.question: that the quarrel is __________ merely about the difficulties,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-** 'Not'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context it is said that the quarrel is not only about the difficulty but also about the aim.
 
• **Not merely **is an idiom which **means** that one thing is true and that another thing is also true.
 
 
• **For example-** He was **not merely** a great baseball player, he was also a great person.
 
 

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is- *That the quarrel is **not merely**__ about the difficulties, but about the aim.*

questions.question: we should tear each ____________ eyes out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Other's".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence it is talking about to tear eyes out where it means that two or more person are involved here.
 
• So, we should use ('s) with other.
 
• An **apostrophe** is a **small punctuation mark ( ' ) placed after a noun** to show the possession. 
 
 
• **For example**- Let’s review each other’s essays **means **my essay and your essay; i.e., two essays
 
 

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is- *We should tear each **other's**__ eyes out.*

questions.question: but some of us would _______ mad with disgust
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Go'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here,** would **is a **modal** Verb.
 
• Modal verbs always come directly **before the main verb** (except for questions).
 
• Modal verbs always take **verb in base form** **(v1 **form).
 
 
• **For example**- I thought he would be here by now.
 
 
 
• So according to above explanation only** 'Go'** is the best suitable choice.
 
• So, verb **'Go'** is the correct answer here. 

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is-* but some of us would **go**__ mad with disgust.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Gone-** V3 form of 'Go'.
 
• **Went-** V2 form of 'Go'.
 
• **Going- **V1+ing form of 'Go'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The report (has already been) given to the Board.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context it is said about submission of report.
 
• We use word** already** in '**Present perfect tense**' so it is clear that answer will be 'Has already been/Have already been'.
 
• The present perfect tense is used in present to indicate the action that has taken place at some specific time.
 
• According to sentence '**The report'** is a **singular** noun so '**Has'** will be used for it.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is- *The report **has already been**__ given to the board. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Sentence Structure** for present perfect tense- **Sub+ has/have+v3+obj.** ​

 
 
• **For example**- We've already had our breakfast.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

You see a curtain of fog (hanged) low, suspended over the fresh green grass
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Hanging'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, the verb see is in **present tense.**
 
• The verb see and the phrase a curtain of fog denotes a **continuous process **indicating that an -ing form verb should be used.
 
• To denote a present continuous tense we should use the** present participle (-ing) form** of the verb.
 
 
• **For example-** The children are going to school.
 
 

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is- *You see a curtain of fog** hanging** low, suspended over the fresh green grass. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hangs-** Used in simple present tense with singular noun.
 
• **Were hang-** hanged, hanging or hung will be used with were instead of hang.
 
• **Hanged-** Used in simple past tense.

questions.question: Mayank remembers that the examination is after 18th December but before 21st December, while Suraj remembers that the examination is before 24th December but after 19th December. On which date of December is the examination?
questions.solution:
Mayank remembers that the examination is after 18th December but before 21st December. So, According to Mayank exam date is 19, **20**

Suraj remembers that the examination is before 24th December but after 19th December. So, According to Suraj exam date is 20, 21, 22, 23

According to both, only 20 December date is common. So, the Exam is on 20 December.

Hence, the examination is on ‘20th December’.

We know,

Error = 1000 - 930 = 70 gms

Gain % = {70 over 1000 - 70}×100

Gain % = {70 over 930}×100

Gain % = 7.53 %

questions.question: Find the potential energy gained by a body of mass 50 kg, if it is raised by 10 m. (use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 5000**__

__**EXPLANATION**__:

The potential energy gained by a body of mass 50 kg, if it is raised by 10m is 5000 Joules.

 Potential energy = mass × acceleration due to gravity(g) × height covered

P.E. = 50 × 10 × 10

= 5000 Joules

Potential energy is the energy possessed by an object because of its position relative to other objects.

questions.question: The relative density of a substance is the _________.

options.text: Ratio of its density to the density of water
Ratio of the density of water to its density
Product of the density of water to its density
Ratio of the volume of water to its volume

questions.solution:
The relative density of a substance is the __**Ratio of its density to the density of water.**__

 
• A substance with a relative density less than 1 will float in water. For example, an ice cube, with a relative density of about 0.91, will float. A substance with a relative density greater than 1 will sink.
 
• If a substance's relative density is less than one then it is less dense than the reference; if greater than 1 then it is denser than the reference(here water)
 
• If the relative density is exactly 1 then the densities are equal; that is, equal volumes of the two substances have the same mass.
